ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Alpine Valley ’82 with smoking Scarlet>Fire and a killer set
ai_show_review.review:
August 8, 1982 at Alpine Valley is one of those late‑summer nights where the Dead seemed to be running on pure adrenaline. The first set rockets off with “Alabama Getaway” into “The Promised Land,” then rolls through a sweet mix of country‑rock and ballads before landing on a soaring “Looks Like Rain” → “Peggy‑O.”  The second set is where the night truly ignites – the classic Scarlet Begonias → Fire transition is on fire, the band rides a blistering “Estimated Prophet,” and the post‑drums jam lifts into an inspired “The Other One.”  Highlights keep coming: a rapturous “They Love Each Other,” a punchy “Good Lovin’,” and a double‑encore that closes with a heartfelt “(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction” → “Brokedown Palace.”  Across the board reviewers note tight playing, soaring solos from Jerry, savage bass work from Phil (even if a few mixes bury it), Brent’s tasteful piano and his signature scratchy tone on “Not Fade Away,” and a thunderous rhythm section powered by Mickey, Bill and occasional guest percussion.  The show is high‑octane throughout, making it a must‑listen for anyone hunting the peak of the ’82 tour.

If you want the cleanest soundboard experience, the Skankweed transfer (gd82-08-08.sbd.skankweed.15580.sbeok.shnf) offers a crisp mix with excellent instrument separation – just be aware that Phil’s bass track is missing, which leaves a slight hole in the low end.  For those who can’t live without the full band sound, the Wise and Barrick SBD recordings capture the bass perfectly and are also superbly engineered.  Either way, this night remains a standout chapter in the Dead’s late‑career catalog.

best_recording.reason: Clean soundboard transfer with crystal‑clear mix; the only drawback is the missing bass track, but overall clarity makes it the most accessible listening source.

key_highlights: Smoking Scarlet Begonias → Fire transition that defines the night
"They Love Each Other" and "Estimated Prophet" showcase peak improvisation
Double‑encore with a soulful Satisfaction → Brokedown Palace finale
Brent Mydland’s scratchy “Not Fade Away” on an excellent audience tape

band_performance.Jerry: On fire all night – blistering solos on Fire and Scarlet, strong (if slightly tired) vocals, and a fiery finish to the set.
band_performance.Phil: Generally solid bass foundation; praised as savage/insane in several recordings, though a few mixes bury him or omit his part entirely.
band_performance.Bob: Earnest vocal delivery on Satisfaction and Good Lovin', providing reliable rhythm guitar throughout.
band_performance.Keys: Brent Mydland delivers tasteful piano on Looks Like Rain and Peggy‑O; his gritty “Not Fade Away” texture is a fan favorite.
band_performance.Drums: Mickey Hart & Bill Kreutzmann lock in tight, especially during the post‑drums jam; guest percussion (Zakir Hussain/Hamza El Din) adds extra sparkle.
